hook: An FBI memo from the Los Angeles field office to Director Hoover documents the Bureau's surveillance of the Amalgamated Flying Saucer Clubs of America (AFSCA) after an IRS employee flagged Issue No. 24 of its journal 'Flying Saucers International' as potentially expounding the Communist Party line — attached with the full magazine issue and UFO newspaper clippings from 1965-1966.
why_it_matters: This file reveals that the FBI treated civilian UFO organizations as potential vectors for Communist subversion during the Cold War, conflating anti-war and anti-Military-Industrial Complex rhetoric (framed as alien transmissions) with Communist Party activity. The document shows the Bureau's surveillance extended to fringe contactee publications, not just military sightings, and that no further action was taken — suggesting the CP angle was quickly dismissed. The attached newspaper clippings, including the Hillsdale Michigan coeds incident and Gary Wilcox egg-shaped craft encounter, were being tracked in the same file as ideological monitoring.
key_findings: An IRS employee, Jarvis H. Cooper of Philadelphia, reported Issue No. 24 of Flying Saucers International to the FBI because pages 2-3 contained an article he believed 'expounded the Communist Party line' — the article was framed as a message from 'Master Kalen-Li Retan, Head of the planet Korendor,' allegedly received by contactee Bob Renaud via shortwave radio on May 4, 1966.

The article explicitly attacks the Vietnam War, calls the US government a 'military puppet' of the Military-Industrial complex, claims President Kennedy was assassinated for opposing it, and argues war is economically profitable — rhetoric the FBI flagged as potentially CP-aligned.

The LA Division confirmed AFSCA's headquarters at 2004 North Hoover Street, Los Angeles, and noted that 'no investigation has ever been conducted on captioned organization' and 'no further action is contemplated' — the matter was closed as informational only.

Newspaper clippings in the file document the March 1966 Hillsdale, Michigan sighting observed by 87 college coeds and their housemother, with Civil Defense Director Van Horn reporting the object was 'about 40 feet wide' with vertical and horizontal movements 'too fast for any airplane,' and the October 1965 Gary Wilcox egg-shaped craft encounter in Newark Valley, NY.

Project Blue Book is referenced in the newspaper clippings as the Air Force program tracking UFO reports, with Selfridge Air Force Base at Mount Clemens, Michigan named as involved in the Hillsdale investigation.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: Newspaper clippings in the file explicitly reference Project Blue Book and Air Force investigation of the March 1966 Michigan sightings, situating this FBI file within the broader interagency UFO tracking apparatus of the era.

The AFSCA magazine article directly names Congress and the White House as facade governments controlled by the Pentagon and defense industries, which was the specific ideological content that triggered FBI review.
